attractions.name: Victoria Falls
attractions.desc: Known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders', this is one of the largest waterfalls in the world by combined width and height. The Zimbabwean side offers the widest, most direct views of the main falls, especially in high water season when spray can be seen for kilometers. Bridge walks and adventure activities like bungee jumping add to the appeal.

attractions.name: Hwange National Park
attractions.desc: Zimbabwe's largest park holds one of Africa's biggest elephant populations, along with strong lion and wild dog numbers. Waterhole-based game viewing is particularly good in the dry season, when animals concentrate around a limited number of pumped water points. It sees far fewer visitors than comparable parks elsewhere in the region.

attractions.name: Mana Pools National Park
attractions.desc: A UNESCO-listed floodplain along the Zambezi River, known for allowing walking safaris in the presence of large game, a rarity in African parks. Elephants, buffalo, and predators gather along the river's pools during the dry season. Its remoteness and strict visitor limits keep it feeling genuinely wild.

attractions.name: Great Zimbabwe ruins
attractions.desc: The stone remains of a medieval city that once anchored a major trading empire, built entirely without mortar from carefully cut granite blocks. It's the largest ancient stone structure in sub-Saharan Africa and gave the country its name. The site includes a hilltop complex and a lower enclosure with massive curved walls.

attractions.name: Lake Kariba
attractions.desc: One of the largest man-made lakes in the world, formed by damming the Zambezi River, now ringed by wildlife-rich shoreline and houseboats. Sunset cruises here are known for close elephant and buffalo sightings as animals come down to drink. It's a relaxed contrast to the more intense game drives elsewhere.

attractions.name: Matobo Hills
attractions.desc: A landscape of huge balancing granite boulders scattered across rolling hills, sacred to local Ndebele and Shona communities and home to ancient rock art. It also holds one of the country's best rhino tracking experiences, done on foot with a guide. Cecil Rhodes chose to be buried here, at a site called World's View.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Victoria Falls
itinerary.desc: The falls themselves, plus optional adventure activities like the bridge walk or a sunset cruise.
itinerary.cost: Zimbabwean-side park entry costs about $30 for foreigners; the bridge walk or bungee adds $50–160.
itinerary.food: Try a proper Zimbabwean sadza dinner at a local restaurant in Victoria Falls town, away from the resort strip.

itinerary.label: Days 3–5
itinerary.title: Hwange National Park
itinerary.desc: Waterhole-based game drives through Zimbabwe's largest wildlife reserve.
itinerary.cost: Bundled into lodge packages, roughly $300–600+/night all-inclusive.
itinerary.food: Meals are included at nearly every Hwange lodge, often built around the day's game-drive schedule.

itinerary.label: Days 6–7
itinerary.title: Matobo Hills
itinerary.desc: Rhino tracking on foot and rock art among giant granite boulders.
itinerary.cost: A guided rhino tracking walk costs about $50–70 per person.
itinerary.food: Pack a picnic for the day — options inside Matobo itself are minimal.

itinerary.label: Day 8
itinerary.title: Great Zimbabwe
itinerary.desc: A stop at the ancient stone ruins before departure from Harare.
itinerary.cost: Site entry costs about $10–15 for foreigners.
itinerary.food: A simple meal in nearby Masvingo is the practical choice before continuing to Harare.

goodToKnow.tipping: USD 10–15/day for safari guides is standard
goodToKnow.safety: Tourist areas around Victoria Falls and the main parks are safe and well set up for visitors
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Domestic flights connect Victoria Falls, Hwange, and Harare; roads elsewhere can be rough
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Victoria Falls Airport (VFA) is the natural start for this route, right by the falls themselves

food.name: Sadza
food.desc: A stiff maize porridge and the country's staple food, usually eaten with a meat or vegetable relish.

food.name: Mopane worms
food.desc: Dried, protein-rich caterpillars, a traditional delicacy across the region.

food.name: Bota
food.desc: A smooth, sweetened maize porridge typically eaten for breakfast.

food.name: Chibuku
food.desc: A traditional fermented sorghum or maize beer, sold and enjoyed widely across the country.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Zimbabwe?
faq.a: Yes, a visa on arrival is available for most nationalities, including the KAZA Univisa, which also covers Zambia.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Victoria Falls Airport (VFA), right by the falls and the natural start for this route.

faq.q: Which side of Victoria Falls is better, Zimbabwe or Zambia?
faq.a: Zimbabwe generally offers more expansive, dramatic views of the main falls face; Zambia gets you closer to the water, including swimming at Devil's Pool in the dry season. The KAZA Univisa lets you see both.
Yes, tourist areas around Victoria Falls and the main parks are well set up and safe for visitors; normal precautions apply as anywhere.

daysReason: 8 days covers Victoria Falls, Hwange, Matobo Hills, and Great Zimbabwe at a solid pace. 5–6 works if you drop one park; 10+ lets you slow the safari legs down.
visa: A visa on arrival (including the KAZA Univisa covering Zambia too) is available for most nationalities — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Cataratas Vitória, lado do Zimbabué
attractions.desc: A margem do Zimbabué oferece vistas mais próximas e molhadas das cataratas, incluindo a emocionante ponte pedonal Knife-Edge, que coloca os visitantes mesmo ao lado da água a cair. Na época seca, a Piscina do Diabo permite nadar mesmo na borda das cataratas. Combina naturalmente com as vistas mais amplas disponíveis do lado zambiano.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Hwange
attractions.desc: Considerado o maior parque do Zimbabué, alberga uma das maiores populações de elefantes de África, junto com fortes números de leões e cães-selvagens. A observação junto a fontes de água é particularmente boa na época seca, quando os animais se concentram à volta de um número limitado de pontos de água bombeada. Recebe muito menos visitantes do que parques comparáveis noutros locais da região.

attractions.name: Colinas de Matobo
attractions.desc: Uma paisagem de enormes rochas de granito em equilíbrio espalhadas por colinas onduladas, sagradas para as comunidades locais Ndebele e Shona e casa de arte rupestre antiga. Também alberga um dos melhores locais de rastreio de rinocerontes do país, feito a pé com um guia. Cecil Rhodes escolheu ser enterrado aqui, num local chamado World's View.

attractions.name: Ruínas do Grande Zimbabué
attractions.desc: Os restos de pedra de uma cidade medieval que outrora ancorou um importante império comercial, construída inteiramente sem argamassa a partir de blocos de granito cuidadosamente cortados. É a maior estrutura antiga de pedra da África subsariana e deu ao país o seu nome. O local inclui um complexo no topo de uma colina e um recinto inferior com muralhas curvas maciças.

attractions.name: Lago Kariba
attractions.desc: Um dos maiores lagos artificiais do mundo, formado pela barragem do Rio Zambeze, hoje rodeado por margens ricas em vida selvagem e casas-barco. Os cruzeiros ao pôr do sol aqui são conhecidos por avistamentos próximos de elefantes e búfalos que descem para beber água. É um contraste relaxante face aos safaris mais intensos noutros locais.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Mana Pools
attractions.desc: Uma planície inundável classificada pela UNESCO ao longo do Rio Zambeze, conhecida por permitir safaris a pé na presença de animais de grande porte, uma raridade em parques africanos. Elefantes, búfalos e predadores reúnem-se junto aos seus poços de água na época seca. A sua condição remota e limites estritos de visitantes mantêm uma sensação de natureza genuinamente selvagem.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Cataratas Vitória
itinerary.desc: As próprias cataratas, mais atividades de aventura opcionais como a caminhada na ponte ou um cruzeiro ao pôr do sol.

itinerary.label: Dias 3–5
itinerary.title: Parque Nacional de Hwange
itinerary.desc: Safaris junto a fontes de água pelo maior parque de vida selvagem do Zimbabué.
itinerary.logistics: ~1,5h de carro desde as Cataratas Vitória

itinerary.label: Dias 6–7
itinerary.title: Colinas de Matobo
itinerary.desc: Rastreio de rinocerontes a pé e arte rupestre entre enormes rochas de granito.
itinerary.logistics: ~4h de carro desde Hwange, via Bulawayo

itinerary.label: Dia 8
itinerary.title: Grande Zimbabué
itinerary.desc: Uma paragem nas antigas ruínas de pedra antes da partida a partir de Harare.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10–15 USD/dia para guias de safári é habitual
goodToKnow.safety: As zonas turísticas à volta das Cataratas Vitória e dos principais parques são seguras e bem preparadas para visitantes
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Voos domésticos ligam Cataratas Vitória, Hwange e Harare; as estradas noutros locais podem ser difíceis
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Victoria Falls Airport (VFA) is the natural start for this route, right by the falls themselves

food.name: Sadza
food.desc: Uma papa firme de milho e o alimento base do país, normalmente comida com um acompanhamento de carne ou legumes.

food.name: Vermes de mopane
food.desc: Lagartas secas e ricas em proteína, uma iguaria tradicional em toda a região.

food.name: Bota
food.desc: Uma papa de milho suave e adoçada, tipicamente comida ao pequeno-almoço.

food.name: Chibuku
food.desc: Uma cerveja tradicional fermentada de sorgo ou milho, vendida e apreciada em todo o país.
